title: Sacred history

rights.policy: Tier-A (public-domain / open / CC0) only. No copyrighted text. Figure metadata, motifs, conventional dates, Wikidata QIDs, and AI-generated contestable correlation claims only.

method: Local-model pipeline (ollama: nomic-embed-text embeddings + llama3.2:3b synthesis). Cross-tradition correlations are AI-generated candidates emitted as contestable claims with evidence and confidence, never as settled fact. $0 paid AI spend.

timeline.label: Composition of the Rigveda
timeline.note: Oral composition of the oldest Vedic hymns; conventionally placed c. 1500-1200 BCE.

timeline.label: Traditional floruit of Zoroaster
timeline.note: Dating ranges widely across scholarship, from the 2nd millennium to the 6th century BCE.

timeline.label: Traditional life of Laozi
timeline.note: Historicity and dates are uncertain; tradition places him as an older contemporary of Confucius.

timeline.label: Life of Confucius
timeline.note: Conventionally 551-479 BCE.

timeline.label: Life of Mahavira
timeline.note: 24th and last Tirthankara of the present age; traditionally c. 599-527 BCE.

timeline.label: Life of Gautama Buddha
timeline.note: Conventional placement c. 6th-5th century BCE; the exact dates remain debated.

timeline.label: Greek translation of the Hebrew scriptures (Septuagint)
timeline.note: Began with the Torah in Alexandria in the 3rd century BCE; the rest followed over the next two centuries.

timeline.label: Life of Jesus of Nazareth
timeline.note: Most scholarship places his birth c. 6-4 BCE and death c. 30-33 CE.

timeline.label: Council of Jerusalem
timeline.note: Early apostolic meeting described in Acts; conventionally dated c. 48-50 CE.

timeline.label: First Council of Nicaea
timeline.note: Convened by Constantine; produced the original Nicene Creed and addressed the dating of Easter.

timeline.label: Council of Chalcedon
timeline.note: Defined the two natures of Christ; a fault line between Chalcedonian and Oriental Orthodox traditions.

timeline.label: Redaction of the Babylonian Talmud
timeline.note: Editorial closing conventionally placed around the 5th-6th century CE.

timeline.label: Life of Muhammad
timeline.note: Conventionally c. 570-632 CE.

timeline.label: The Hijra (migration to Medina)
timeline.note: Year 1 of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.

timeline.label: Compilation of the Uthmanic codex of the Qur'an
timeline.note: Standardization of the consonantal text under the caliph Uthman, conventionally c. 650 CE.

timeline.label: Life of Guru Nanak
timeline.note: Founder of Sikhism, 1469-1539 CE.

timeline.label: Compilation of the Adi Granth
timeline.note: First compilation of the Sikh scripture by Guru Arjan.

timeline.label: Publication of the Book of Mormon
timeline.note: Published by Joseph Smith; founding text of the Latter Day Saint movement.

timeline.label: Declaration of Baha'u'llah
timeline.note: Baha'u'llah's declaration of his mission, conventionally dated to 1863 in Baghdad.

timeline.label: Discovery of the Nag Hammadi library
timeline.note: A cache of early Christian and Gnostic codices found in Upper Egypt.

timeline.label: Discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls
timeline.note: Manuscripts found in the Qumran caves, including some of the oldest surviving Hebrew biblical texts.
